title: Version Control and Collaboration knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Version Control and Collaboration”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Storing scripts in Git” under lesson 166, “Version Control and Collaboration”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Version Control and Collaboration”?
options: Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Combine static analysis with repeatable behavior tests and code review.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
questions.answer_key: Combine static analysis with repeatable behavior tests and code review.
questions.explanation: Combine static analysis with repeatable behavior tests and code review. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Version Control and Collaboration”?
options: Declare the target interpreter and test the feature set on the oldest supported environment.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
questions.answer_key: Declare the target interpreter and test the feature set on the oldest supported environment.
questions.explanation: Declare the target interpreter and test the feature set on the oldest supported environment. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
